title: New Jersey Attorney General Opens Civil Rights Investigation into Delaney Hall ICE Facility
excerpt: New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport issued investigative subpoenas against Delaney Hall detention center, launching a civil rights investigation into whether GEO Group employees violated detainees' rights amid a string of deaths and reports of denied medical care.
content:
On August 7, 2026, New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport announced that the state's Division on Civil Rights had issued investigative subpoenas to Delaney Hall in Newark, a private immigration detention facility operated by The GEO Group, Inc.

  • The investigation focuses on whether GEO Group employees violated detainees' civil rights, following mounting reports of poor conditions and multiple deaths.
  • The investigation came less than a week after the death of Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, the third detainee death connected to Delaney Hall since May 2025.
  • Gov. Mikie Sherrill noted that ICE and GEO Group had blocked efforts for a full health inspection and that visitations had been stopped.
  • The New Jersey AG had previously filed a separate lawsuit seeking court-ordered access for health inspectors, after GEO Group denied state health officials entry to the facility.

"New Jersey has both a legal and a moral duty to stand up for the civil rights of people within our state," Attorney General Davenport said. The civil rights investigation was the first state-level enforcement action targeting an ICE contract facility in response to detainee deaths under the second Trump administration.
source: New Jersey Office of Attorney General
